result_text:
Template literals are now blanked out when units are compared for duplication, so two JavaScript functions that differ only inside a `` `...` `` literal are reported as one duplicated unit. I didn't add a test for the new behavior, and I didn't run a JavaScript example through the duplication report. The `codeanalyzer` module tests ran with no errors reported.

The change is one line in `extraCleanContent` in `codeanalyzer/.../units/CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java`. It replaces `` `...` `` with ` `` ` before the other string-literal replacements run, which also keeps a `'` or `"` inside a template from being matched first. A difference in code outside the literals still keeps the units apart.

Like the existing `"..."` and `'...'` handling, this works one line at a time. A template literal that spans several lines isn't normalized, so two units that differ only inside a multi-line template are still treated as different. I left it that way because collapsing lines would break the line numbers reported for units.

I haven't committed anything.
